title: Types Overview
narrative:
## XIOM's Type System

Every value in XIOM has a **type** — a label that tells the compiler what kind of data it is. XIOM is **statically typed**, meaning types are checked before your program runs, catching mistakes early.

### The Five Core Types

| Type | What It Holds | Example |
|------|---------------|--------|
| `Int` | Whole numbers (64-bit) | `42`, `-7`, `0` |
| `Float64` | Decimal numbers | `3.14`, `-0.5`, `2.0` |
| `Bool` | True or false | `true`, `false` |
| `Char` | A single character | `'a'`, `'7'`, `'\n'` |
| `Str` | Text (string of characters) | `"hello"`, `"XIOM"` |

### Declaring Variables with Types

You can explicitly specify a type using `var`:

```xiom
var age: Int = 25;
var price: Float64 = 19.99;
var is_ready: Bool = true;
var initial: Char = 'X';
var greeting: Str = "Hello, world!";
```

Or let XIOM **infer** the type with `let`:

```xiom
let age = 25;           // XIOM knows this is Int
let price = 19.99;      // XIOM knows this is Float64
let greeting = "Hi!";   // XIOM knows this is Str
```

### Type Checking Prevents Bugs

XIOM won't let you mix types accidentally:

```xiom
let x: Int = 42;
// let y: Str = x;  // ERROR: can't put an Int into a Str
```

This catches mistakes at compile time instead of runtime!
tips: Use `var` with an explicit type when you want to be clear about your intent
Use `let` for cleaner code — XIOM infers the type automatically
Char literals use single quotes `'X'`, Str literals use double quotes `"X"`
Bool has only two values: `true` and `false`
